author: reek
body: The browser face of idea-forge, built as a widget tree and compiled through the HTML plug -- no hand-written HTML. The page walks the reservation protocol: state your name and your demand, the house deals three candidate fortunes, you reserve exactly one, and the other two return to the deck. Below the table sits the ledger -- every fortune already reserved, so customers can see the house never deals the same idea twice. Field display is a light text scan over response bodies the server composed as JsonValue trees.

author: reek
body: Pulls named fields out of a raw response body for display. The service's strings contain no embedded quotes, so scanning to the next quote is exact. The nth variant walks repeated keys, which is how the three candidates and the ledger rows are read out of their arrays without a JSON parser in the page.

author: reek
body: Percent-encodes only the characters that would break the query string; the service's url-decode handles the rest. Percent must be replaced first so later replacements are not double-encoded.

author: reek
body: The dealing and claiming flags make the buttons single-shot: a second click while a request is in flight is ignored outright, so a double-click can never burn the daily deal or clobber a live offer. Error responses land in the notice strip; they never replace an offer already on the table.

author: reek
body: The full tree mounts exactly once. Every update after boot re-mounts only the dynamic region (notice, table, ledger), so the header and the input panel never flash and never lose focus or typed text.
